The problem

Two things can close a behavioral-health clinic: burnout, and a failed audit.

Clinicians lose hours a day to documentation while payers and accreditors demand ever more rigor. One denied-claim trend or a failed state survey can shut a facility down — and the paperwork that prevents it is the same paperwork burning out your team.

Documentation

Finish the note before you leave the room.

Record the session, dictate after, type live, or document a phone call — and start from a structured draft instead of a blank page. You correct what's wrong and sign. Nothing enters the record without a clinician's name on it.

  • ✓ Your words anchor the note; the draft never overrides them
  • ✓ Co-signature routing handled for supervised staff
  • ✓ Typing every note yourself is always a first-class path
The day

Everyone opens Kura to their own job.

A front-desk day and a clinical day have nothing in common, so they don't share a screen. Each role gets a workspace built around its actual work — and sees only what that work requires.

  • ✓ Clinicians, nurses, front desk, intake, case management, billing, leadership
  • ✓ What needs you today, in one list — not buried in menus
  • ✓ Access scoped by role, enforced server-side and recorded
Audit readiness

It runs the survey before the surveyor does.

Kura reads your charts the way a regulator would and tells you what a survey would find — while there is still time to fix it. Answers come from the record, with their evidence shown; where the record can't support an answer, it says so instead of guessing.

Answers from the record

Findings trace back to what is actually documented — not an impression, and not a confident guess.

Honest about gaps

Where the chart doesn't support a conclusion, that is what it reports. No “you'll pass” that isn't earned.

A human decides

Every finding is reviewed and dispositioned by your team. The system informs the judgment; it doesn't replace it.

app.kurahealth.ai
Built for real PHI, from day one

Behavioral health has stricter rules. We designed for them first.

Substance-use records carry federal protections beyond ordinary health privacy. A system that treats them like any other note puts the clinic at risk — so those obligations shaped the architecture rather than being bolted on afterwards.

42 CFR Part 2 aware

The stricter confidentiality regime for substance-use records is modeled in the product, not left to staff memory.

Least-privilege access

People see what their job requires. That includes us: our own staff hold no standing access to your patients' charts.

Everything recorded

Views, edits, signatures and disclosures are logged — so the clinic can always answer who did what, and when.

Signed, never silently edited

A signed clinical record is permanent; corrections are additions with their own history. That's the legal standard.

Two-factor sign-in

Optional or clinic-wide, with recovery paths designed so security never turns into a lockout.

Sensitive charts stay sensitive

Employee and VIP records can be sealed from ordinary view, with a documented, time-limited path for genuine need.
